intake.replay_rule: Replay only the six manifest-listed files from the source snapshot into repository-relative paths; verify source and destination SHA-256 equality before any semantic action. Do not copy or reconstruct legacy v0.1 files.

internal_contract.identity_rule: The identity key is namespace plus semantic atom id plus version; v0.3 research records are immutable source evidence and any runtime record is a new v0.4 record with an explicit supersedes reference.
internal_contract.public_projection_rule: Compile and validate typed atoms internally first; project only canonical string atom ids, existing instructions/reads/gates/stops, evidence citations, conflicts, and receipt string fields into current public contracts. A failed typed compile never falls back to a generic atom when a domain obligation is required.

rationale: The v0.3 contract is research evidence, not a runtime-compatible public schema; adding a typed internal projection preserves the existing 0.5.7 public tool and packet contracts while allowing fail-closed typed validation.

The existing packet and receipt schemas already carry string atom ids, gates, stops, verification results, and evidence citations, so a new public version is not required for the first vertical slice.
A deliberately new public version would expand the compatibility surface before runtime behavior, evaluator validity, provider preflight, and cross-skill composition are proven.
An internal contract version makes semantic changes explicit: no v0.3 source record is silently mutated and no legacy string is promoted to a domain atom.

input: explicit SemanticContext with objective, task identity, phase, inputs, reads, and evidence state
rule: Positive requires a domain-owned semantic signal plus every required input; literal word matches are not sufficient.
Negative rejects the atom without emitting its domain obligations.
Ambiguous produces hold_for_evidence and a stop when required ownership, input, read, or evidence is absent.
Phase incompatibility is negative; missing or contradictory phase is ambiguous or a hard stop according to the atom contract.
Dependencies are resolved before dependents; a missing or rejected dependency blocks the dependent.
Conflicts are explicit typed relations with a declared resolution or stop; order and wording never silently choose a winner.
Generic process atoms can support a domain atom but cannot replace it.
Workflow/route selection can request atom ids but cannot override compiler rejection or hold.
Canonical order is dependency depth, required-before-optional, family, then full versioned id; lexical order is only a final tie-breaker.
The render target must be packet, receipt, or advisory trace; provider prompts and provider outcomes are forbidden targets.
Every projected domain id retains its source citation and trust class in the internal trace even when the public field is a string.

output: budget stop if required set cannot fit
rule: Required domain atoms and their required dependencies are reserved before optional process or domain atoms.
Optional selection ranks semantic obligation coverage and evidence utility, then uses canonical id for deterministic ties.
A required set exceeding the local budget is a hold/stop, not truncation or silent substitution.
The estimate is local planning data, never provider token telemetry or an economics claim.
Typed ids are projected only after compilation; a required typed stop blocks admission rather than being hidden in a generic atom.
The existing packet builder remains the public rendering owner and its caps remain enforced.
No new public packet property is required in the first slice; typed provenance remains in the internal advisory trace and existing citation/conflict fields.
A missing internal semantic bundle leaves the current legacy composition path unchanged.

output: unchanged advisory trust and override policy
rule: Receipt fields remain strings under tmcp-run-receipt-v0.1; typed ids and concise verification statements are projected without changing the schema.
Untrusted harvested or provider text cannot upgrade a receipt or satisfy a typed obligation.
A receipt records what was compiled/projected and verified; it does not prove provider outcomes or causal value.
The typed-static variant validates contract decisions and public projection only; it does not execute a provider cell.
Fixture labels are held out and tuning-disabled; they may validate implementation behavior but cannot tune atoms or establish efficacy.
Invalid arms must remain rejected before any outcome cell and cross-skill composition remains a separate closed gate.
No automatic promotion, admission, production, economic, or causal claim is emitted.

applicability: positive => admit only when semantic predicates, required inputs, reads, and evidence are all satisfied
negative => reject and emit no domain obligations
ambiguous => hold_for_evidence, emit the missing-evidence stop, and do not admit a generic substitute
fail_closed_policy.domain_without_trigger_words: A domain atom may admit when explicit semantic context and owned evidence satisfy its contract even if no literal trigger word appears. Literal lexical matches can nominate a candidate only; they cannot provide the semantic signal, ownership, or evidence required for admission.
fail_closed_policy.phase: The compiler requires an explicit compatible phase. A phase mismatch rejects the atom; a missing, contradictory, or unowned phase holds/stops when the atom is required.
fail_closed_policy.required_reads: Every required read must resolve to an allowed source reference and be present in the semantic context. An unresolved or unauthorized read holds/stops the atom and cannot be replaced by an excerpt or path-name match.
fail_closed_policy.evidence: Each evidence obligation must have a source-scoped, trust-allowed evidence record. Missing, stale, contradictory, or ownerless evidence is not inferred from labels and produces hold/stops.
fail_closed_policy.verification: Verification obligations require an observable result or an explicitly recorded not-run state. A plan, hash, or provider text is not itself a successful verification result.
fail_closed_policy.stop_conditions: A required stop condition blocks typed admission and is projected to the existing packet gates/stops and receipt verification fields. Stops are not advisory prose that can be removed by token selection.
fail_closed_policy.trust: Trusted committed contracts and sealed fixtures can define semantics; harvested text, provider/model output, legacy strings, and third-party context are untrusted inputs and cannot upgrade applicability or provenance.
fail_closed_policy.cost: Estimated local cost is validated before projection. If required atoms plus dependencies exceed the local budget, the compiler holds/stops; it never truncates required obligations or substitutes a generic atom.
fail_closed_policy.unresolved_dependencies: A missing, rejected, ambiguous, or conflicting dependency blocks its dependent; topological ordering does not make an unresolved dependency valid.
fail_closed_policy.conflicts: A declared conflict must have an explicit typed resolution or produce a stop. Lexical priority, workflow order, source order, and token budget are not conflict resolution.

legacy_string_atoms.normalization: For internal bookkeeping only, normalize the original UTF-8 string to legacy.string.<first-16-hex-sha256>; preserve the exact original string for public projection.
legacy_string_atoms.semantic_status: legacy_string, generic/process-only, never a typed domain atom
legacy_string_atoms.admission: Legacy strings may continue through the existing compatibility path, but cannot satisfy a typed domain obligation, dependency, evidence obligation, verification obligation, or conflict resolution.
legacy_string_atoms.mixed_input: Compile typed records and legacy strings in separate namespaces. Do not fuzzy-merge, infer a typed record from a legacy collision, or let a legacy string satisfy a required domain atom.
legacy_string_atoms.projection_order: Preserve the existing legacy atom sequence exactly; append newly admitted typed ids in canonical typed order without evicting existing strings. If the public cap would omit a required typed id, hold/stop instead of silently evicting or truncating it.
legacy_string_atoms.collision: A same-text or same-slug legacy string never wins over a versioned typed id and never changes the typed id's provenance.

migration_rules: Create a new internal v0.4 record with a supersedes reference for each runtime-seeded v0.3 atom; never edit or reinterpret the v0.3 research artifact in place.
Seed the first slice only with H1's data_integrity.reconciliation and migration_readiness.rollback_path plus the generic process shell; defer the other six domain atoms to a later versioned decision.
Keep the typed compiler behind an internal opt-in semantic-bundle path. With no bundle, the current lexical/legacy composition behavior remains the baseline.
Project only fields already represented by current public packet and receipt contracts; preserve exact legacy strings and existing public ordering when the typed path is absent.
Treat any semantic field change, new family, new conflict resolution, public field, or public tool argument as a new decision version rather than an additive patch to v0.4.
rollback_rules: If baseline compose output or the public contract fixture changes when the internal bundle is absent, disable the typed path and stop the slice.

If any typed registry, applicability, dependency, conflict, read, evidence, trust, stop, or budget gate fails, return the current legacy path only when no required typed domain obligation was requested; otherwise return hold/stop with no generic substitution.
Rollback removes the compose/evaluator adapter call sites before removing the new pure module; no public schema migration, receipt migration, package install, or data purge is allowed.
A subsequent runtime record version must carry a new decision packet and explicit migration map; do not mutate v0.4 identities in place.

smallest_implementation_slice.goal: Prove one opt-in, pure typed compiler path from durable v0.3 semantics through H1 applicability, dependency/conflict resolution, local budget selection, existing packet/receipt projection, and advisory static evaluation without changing a public contract or running a provider cell.
ordered_changes: Add immutable typed models, registry validation, explicit v0.3-to-v0.4 supersedes refs, and the H1 seed records in the new pure domain module.
Define SemanticContext as explicit inputs/evidence/phase/read state; allow a lexical candidate to enter consideration but never to satisfy a domain predicate.
Implement fail-closed applicability, dependency/conflict resolution, phase/read/evidence/trust/stop checks, and deterministic local budget selection.
Implement RenderRecord plus packet and receipt projections that feed existing string fields and preserve current public schemas and legacy ordering.
Add an opt-in internal compose adapter; when no explicit semantic bundle is supplied, assert byte-equivalent legacy behavior and do not activate typed atoms.
Register one non-provider typed-static advisory evaluation variant and score compiler decisions/traces against the sealed fixtures; do not invoke provider cells or auto-promotion.
Run the focused runtime/projection tests, public-contract tests, full suite, quality gates, and whitespace checks before any provider preflight request.
